summary: Insurance product information document (IPID) for easyPROTECT-Auto, published under the banner “Motor vehicle insurance - Vehicles other than cars and motorhomes” and the product line “LALUX Assurances - Product : easyPROTECT-Auto”. The document states that easyPROTECT-Auto covers motor vehicle third party liability as well as damage caused to the vehicle, and sets out seven guarantees: civil liability, legal protection (costs and fees up to EUR 10,000), fire, theft, glass breakage, damage to the vehicle, and an optional accessory driver’s guarantee reserved for van type vehicles. Cover applies in the countries indicated on the green card, with an explicit 42-territory list for damage to the vehicle, and the contract runs from year to year by tacit renewal.

gaps: Insurer: the document prints the brand “LALUX Assurances” in the title banner (with the “lalux ASSURANCES” logo) and the line “LALUX Assurances - Product : easyPROTECT-Auto”; the body then refers only to “the company” and “the insurance company”. No legal form, no RCS number, no registered address and no authorisation reference appear on either page, so this document alone does not identify which authorised entity carries the risk. `insurer_name` carries the printed brand “LALUX Assurances” rather than the task metadata value “lalux”.

Divergence recorded without arbitration: the “Special provisions per guarantee:” block on page 2 names a guarantee “Collision with a stray animal” and gives its claims formalities, but no guarantee of that name is listed or described in the “What is insured  ?” box on page 1. It is recorded as a separate coverage cited to page 2, with `is_optional`, `territorial_scope` and `limits` left null, and its description states that the guarantee is known only from that block. Nothing was borrowed from the French or German version of the same IPID to describe it.

No edition date, no version number and no internal reference is printed on either page: `edition_date` and `reference` are null. The PDF file metadata carry a creation and modification date of 2018-10-08 14:11:22+02:00, the producer “Adobe InDesign CC 13.1 (Macintosh)” and the source file name “IPID_Assurance Auto_LALUX_easyPROTECT-Auto_Véhicules Type 2_EN.indd”. These are file metadata, not printed content, and were not taken as an edition date; they are noted because a 2018 IPID may describe a product no longer sold in this form. The InDesign file name is also the only place the “Type 2” designation of the task metadata appears; the printed document says only “Vehicles other than cars and motorhomes”.

Product identity: the banner prints the document title “Motor vehicle insurance  -  Vehicles other than cars and motorhomes” over “Insurance Product Information Document”, and the product line reads “LALUX Assurances - Product : easyPROTECT-Auto”. `product_name` therefore carries “easyPROTECT-Auto”, the commercial name the document itself gives as the product, `product_family` the same value, and `variant` carries the printed sub-title “Vehicles other than cars and motorhomes” (a parallel IPID exists for the other vehicle type, in the same three languages). `is_extension` is false.

`is_optional`: the six guarantees printed under “Vehicle insurance guarantees:” (Civil liability, Legal protection, Fire, Theft, Glass breakage, Damage to the vehicle) are recorded as not optional, and the “Driver’s guarantee” printed under the heading “Optional accessory guarantee / Only for van type vehicles:” as optional. The document nowhere states in so many words that the first six are included by default: the false value reflects only the printed contrast between the two headings, plus the sentence “easyPROTECT-Auto is an insurance that covers your motor vehicle third party liability as well as the damage caused to your vehicle”, which names two of the six. Nothing was deduced from what motor policies usually contain.

The only monetary amounts in the whole document are EUR 10,000 (legal protection costs and fees), EUR 500 (the floor below which legal proceedings for recovery are restricted) and the 1.2 g per litre blood alcohol threshold of the drink-driving exclusion. No sum insured, no civil liability ceiling, no deductible amount and no premium figure is printed: `deductibles.standard` is null and only `deductibles.variable` carries the document's own wording “In some cases, deductibles apply, e.g. when the driver has caused an accident under the influence of alcohol”. The currency is written “EUR” in words in this document, so no € glyph was involved.

The box “Are there any restrictions on cover ?” holds five items, none of which is an excluded event: a premium increase after a liability claim, a EUR 500 floor for recovery proceedings, replacement of glass only when technically necessary, a cap on labour costs at Luxembourg rates, and deductibles in some cases. Following the convention of the other easyPROTECT extraction in this batch, each is recorded in `exclusions` (because that is the box the document prints them in, and the box is titled as a restriction) with its nature stated in the description, and each is also reflected in the corresponding coverage's `limits`, `deductible` or `conditions`, or in `premium.notes`, so that neither reading is lost.

Structure and recount: the bullets are images and produce no text. Counting them by size closes exactly against what was extracted — page 1: 12 green ticks (7.2 x 7.9 pt), 5 red crosses (7.2 x 7.2 pt) and 5 orange exclamation marks (2.4 x 8.9 pt); page 2: 2 ticks for the two territorial bullets. The 12 green ticks are grouped by the document under 7 bold guarantee headings (Civil liability 2, Legal protection 1, Fire 2, Theft 2, Glass breakage 1, Damage to the vehicle 3, Driver’s guarantee 1); `coverages` follows those 7 headings, with every one of the 12 printed bullets reproduced inside the corresponding `description`, plus the eighth coverage known only from page 2. The 5 red crosses are the 5 entries in `exclusions` that carry no “Are there any restrictions on cover ?” marker; the 5 orange marks are the other 5.

`definitions` is empty: the document has no glossary and defines no term. “Green card”, “bonus-malus degree”, “van type vehicles” and “beneficiaries” are all used without a definition; the bonus-malus is mentioned three times (as a certificate to be supplied at subscription, as a premium increase after a liability claim and as a certificate to be issued on cancellation) but the mechanism is never described.

The two territorial bullets do not have the same scope and the document does not reconcile them: “In the countries indicated on the green card” is stated for the contract, while the Damage to the vehicle guarantee carries its own explicit list of 42 territories. The list is recorded verbatim as that guarantee's `territorial_scope`; the green-card wording is used for the other guarantees, which is what the box prints, and the document does not say which countries are on the green card.

Typographic anomalies kept verbatim and not corrected: “What is insured  ?” carries two thin spaces before the question mark where every other heading carries one; “Motor vehicle insurance  -  ” has doubled spaces around the hyphen; “Fire, lightening strikes, explosions” prints “lightening” for “lightning”; the coverage bullet refers to the “Vehicle damage” coverage while the guarantee heading reads “Damage to the vehicle”; the premium obligation says the company can “suspend the warranties” where “guarantees” is meant elsewhere; and the list under “During the contractual period” mixes bullet markers, one U+2022 followed by two hyphens, which a 2.4x render confirms is what the page prints.

Text-layer checks, all clean on this file: both pages re-extracted with page.get_text("text") via PyMuPDF are character-for-character identical to the text pasted into the prompt (the prompt was not truncated; the document is 2 pages); no text block outside the page rectangle, no zero-width space, no soft hyphen, no NFD accent, no private-use glyph, no U+0007, no lost ligature, no duplicated or hidden text layer. The only unusual characters are 10 thin spaces U+2009 before “?” and “:”, 3 curly apostrophes U+2019, 2 en dashes U+2013 inside the Driver’s guarantee sentence and the curly double quotes around “Vehicle damage”. Page 1 bullets are a bare tab, page 2 bullets a U+2022 or a hyphen followed by a tab. These characters sit inside several `key_quotes` and were preserved as exact spans cut from the PDF, never retyped.

Reading order of the text layer differs from the printed layout, without any content being lost: page.get_text("text") returns the three grey boxes first and only then the disclaimer, the “What type of insurance is it ?” paragraph and the title banner, which are printed at the top of page 1.
